Antonio Delgado as LG |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2022/05/hochul-taps-upstate-rep-antonio-delgado-lg/366415/ |access-date=May 3, 2022 |website=[[City & State]]}}{{cite news |last1=Fandos |first1=Nicholas |last2=Ferre-Sadurni |first2=Luis |title=Hochul Chooses Antonio Delgado as New Lieutenant Governor |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/05/03/nyregion/antonio-delgado-new-york-lieutenant-governor-hochul.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=May 3, 2022 |access-date=May 3, 2022 |issn=0362-4331}} Democratic nominee [[Pat Ryan (politician)|Pat Ryan]] defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee [[Marc Molinaro]] in what was seen as an [[Upset (competition)|upset]] due to Molinaro's lead in polls and fundraising in the weeks leading to the election.{{cite news |title=Democrats hold onto key House seat in N.Y. special election |first=Andrew |last=Solender |work=[[Axios Cash on hand |- | {{party shading/Republican}}| Marc Molinaro (R) | $1,593,762 | $993,626 | $600,136 |- | {{party shading/Democratic}}| Pat Ryan (D) | $1,582,369 | $1,265,848 | $316,522 |- ! colspan="4"| Source: [[OpenSecrets]]{{Cite web |title=New York District 19 2022 Special Election |url=https://www.opensecrets.org/races/special-elections-summary?cycle=2022&id=NY19 |access-date=August 24, 2022 |website=[[OpenSecrets]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220824085920/https://www.opensecrets.org/races/special-elections-summary?cycle=2022&id=NY19 |archive-date=August 24, 2022 |language=en}} |} ===Results=== Pat Ryan won the election with 66,088 votes or 51.2% of the vote compared to Marc Molinaro's 48.8% of the vote or 63,010 votes. This defied most polls, which had Molinaro winning by a somewhat comfortable margin as well as Sabato's Crystal Ball rating of Lean R. His victory can be attributed to his large margins in [[Ulster County, New York|Ulster County]]. Ryan overperformed [[Joe Biden]]'s [[2020 United States presidential election in New York|2020]] margin in this district by about 0.8%. The result was considered an upset by some, as Molinaro had led by as much as 14 percentage points in public polling of the race, and Molinaro outspent Ryan on television advertising.{{Cite web |title=Democrats win Albany-area special House race despite being outspent on airwaves |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/meet-the-press/meetthepressblog/democrats-win-albany-area-special-house-race-outspent-airwaves-rcna44569 |access-date=2022-08-24 |website=NBC News |date=August 24, 2022 |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Solender |first=Andrew |date=2022-08-24 |title=Democrats hold onto key House seat in N.Y. special election as Pat Ryan wins |url=https://www.axios.com/2022/08/24/pat-ryan-new-york-special-election |access-date=2022-08-24 |website=Axios |language=en}} Ryan's victory led some forecasters to change some of their predictions for the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|2022 House election]].{{Cite web |title=Red Wave Looks More Like a Ripple |url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/analysis/house/2022-primaries/red-wave-looks-more-ripple |access-date=2022-08-24 |website=Cook Political Report |date=August 24, 2022 |language=en}} Ultimately, the special election foreshadowed 2022 would not go on to be a red wave, as while Republicans would narrowly flip the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]], they would [[2022 United States Senate election|lose a seat in the United States Senate]].{{cite news |title=Understanding the Outcome of the 2022 US Midterms
